# tissue_mast_probe (Resource)

A probe: Mast checks a URL, port, certificate, DNS name, host or mail server from several locations on a schedule, and pages when they agree it is down. The conditions you leave out are not checked, so the configuration is the whole check. `name`, `interval_secs`, `paused` and `domain_expiry` follow the app when you leave them out.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Checks the health endpoint every minute and pages the ops alert source when it stops answering 200.
resource "tissue_mast_probe" "shop" {
  name            = "shop"
  target          = "https://shop.example.com/health"
  interval_secs   = 60
  expect_status   = 200
  body_contains   = "ok"
  max_ms          = 2000
  host            = "web1"
  alert_source_id = tissue_mast_alert_source.ops.id
}

# The MX records have to be exactly these two.
resource "tissue_mast_probe" "mx" {
  kind       = "dns"
  target     = "example.com"
  method     = "MX"
  expect_set = "mx1.example.com,mx2.example.com"
}

# Postgres must not be reachable from outside. This pages when the port opens.
resource "tissue_mast_probe" "db_closed" {
  kind   = "tcp"
  target = "db.example.com:5432"
  expect = "down"
}

# An endpoint behind a token. Keep the token in a variable, not in the file.
resource "tissue_mast_probe" "api" {
  target = "https://api.example.com/v1/status"
  auth = {
    type  = "bearer"
    token = var.status_token
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `target` (String) What to check: a URL for `http`, `host:port` for `tcp`, `tls` and `smtp`, a name for `dns`, a host for `icmp`. Mast keeps one probe per check, so a second probe with the same kind, target, method and conditions is refused.

### Optional

- `alert_source_id` (String) The alert source the probe's pages go to, `mc_...`.
- `auth` (Attributes) `http`: credentials to send. Mast never gives the secret back, so Terraform can't see it change in the app, and after an import the first apply sends it again. Mast sends credentials only to a domain you have proven yours. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth))
- `body_contains` (String) Text the answer must contain: the response body for `http`, a record for `dns`, the server's reply for `smtp` and `tcp`.
- `body_not_contains` (String) `http`: text the response body must not contain.
- `channel_id` (String, Deprecated) The deprecated name of `alert_source_id`.
- `domain_expiry` (Boolean) Whether Mast watches the registration of the target's domain and sends a notice when it has 30, 14 and 7 days left. On unless you turn it off; `true` is refused on a plan without domain expiry notices and for a target with no registered domain, such as an IP address.
- `expect` (String) `up` (the default), or `down` for a target that should not answer: the probe is fine while the check fails and pages when it succeeds.
- `expect_header` (String) `http`: `Name: text`, a header the response must carry with `text` in its value. `Name:` alone only asks that it's there.
- `expect_set` (String) `dns`: the exact set of records the answer must hold, comma-separated.
- `expect_status` (Number) `http`: the one status that counts as up. Without it, or `expect_statuses`, any 2xx or 3xx does.
- `expect_statuses` (String) `http`: the statuses that count as up, comma-separated, such as `200,204`. Replaces `expect_status`.
- `expect_value` (String) `http`: the value at `json_path`, as JSON or a bare string. `dns`: a record the answer must hold.
- `host` (String) The machine the target runs on, such as `web1`, so a page can say what else is wrong on it. Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.
- `ignore_case` (Boolean) Match text without regard to case.
- `interval_secs` (Number) Seconds between checks, 300 unless you say otherwise. The plan sets the shortest interval, and a probe on port 25 checks at most every 300 seconds.
- `json_path` (String) `http`: a path into a JSON response body, `/a/0/b` or `a.0.b`, that must exist.
- `kind` (String) What the probe does: `http` (the default), `tcp`, `tls`, `dns`, `icmp` or `smtp`. Changing it replaces the probe.
- `max_ms` (Number) An answer that takes longer than this many milliseconds, up to 60000, is `slow`: it shows on the probe and pages nobody.
- `method` (String) For `http` the request method: `GET` (the default), `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT` or `PATCH`. For `dns` the record type: `A` (the default), `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `TXT` or `NS`. For `smtp` how far to go after the banner: `EHLO` or `STARTTLS`; leave it out to stop at the banner.
- `name` (String) The name shown in the app and on a page. Defaults to the target's host name.
- `paused` (Boolean) A paused probe makes no checks and sends nothing.
- `policy_id` (String) The escalation policy the probe's pages follow, `po_...`.
- `request_body` (String) `http` with `POST`, `PUT` or `PATCH`: the body to send, up to 16 KiB. Mast sends one only to a domain you have proven yours.
- `request_content_type` (String) `http`: the Content-Type of `request_body`. `application/json` when a body comes without one.
- `request_headers` (List of String) `http`: headers to send, each one `Name: value`, at most 10.
- `resolver` (String) `dns`: the resolver to ask, a public IP address with an optional port.
- `send` (String) `tcp`: text to send once connected, with `\r`, `\n`, `\t` and `\\` decoded. The reply is matched against `body_contains`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the probe was made.
- `id` (String) The probe id, `pr_...`.

<a id="nestedatt--auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth`

Required:

- `type` (String) `basic` or `bearer`.

Optional:

- `password` (String, Sensitive) `basic`: the password.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) `bearer`: the token.
- `username` (String) `basic`: the user name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import tissue_mast_probe.shop shop
terraform import tissue_mast_probe.shop pr_5d1c0e7a9b3f4c26
```
